title: Bug: Flaky standalone tunnel route test due to arp_update interference
author: sireesha-n-arista
body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

Medium

### Description of the bug

The `test_standalone_tunnel_route` test fails intermittently because the
background `arp_update` process runs while the test is creating an unresolved
IPv6 neighbor.

In the failed runs, orchagent creates the required tunnel route, removes it
almost immediately, and creates it again about five seconds later. The test
packets are sent while the route is missing, so PTF does not receive the
expected tunneled packet.

The logs show that orchagent/MuxOrch removes the route. They do not show
`arp_update` directly deleting the route.


### Steps to Reproduce

1. Run the following test on a Dual-ToR testbed:

   `tests/dualtor/test_standalone_tunnel_route.py::test_standalone_tunnel_route`

2. Run the test multiple times in a loop.
3. Check the DUT syslog and PTF packet verification result.
4. In a failed run, observe the following sequence:
   - `arp_update` tries to reach the unresolved IPv6 neighbor.
   - Orchagent creates the standalone tunnel route.
   - Orchagent immediately removes the route.
   - Orchagent creates the route again about five seconds later.
   - PTF does not receive the expected tunneled packet.

### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

### Actual Behavior
The standalone tunnel route is removed while the test packets are being sent.
PTF fails with:
`AssertionError: Did not receive expected packet on any of ports`
Before the fix, 2 out of 30 loop runs failed with the same log sequence.

### Expected Behavior
The background `arp_update` process should not change the neighbor state while
this test is checking standalone tunnel routing.
The tunnel route should remain available while the test packets are sent, and
PTF should receive the expected IP-in-IP packet.


### Relevant log output

```shell
2026 Aug 27 09:27:48.618913 gd272 WARNING swss#arp_update:
command failed after 1 retries: ndisc6 on Vlan1000 to fc02:1000::1f4

2026 Aug 27 09:27:48.902103 gd272 NOTICE swss#orchagent:
create_route: Created tunnel route to fc02:1000::1f4/128

2026 Aug 27 09:27:48.902531 gd272 NOTICE swss#orchagent:
removeStandaloneTunnelRoute: Removing standalone tunnel route for neighbor fc02:1000::1f4

2026 Aug 27 09:27:48.903399 gd272 NOTICE swss#orchagent:
remove_route: Removed tunnel route to fc02:1000::1f4/128

2026 Aug 27 09:27:53.984435 gd272 NOTICE swss#orchagent:
create_route: Created tunnel route to fc02:1000::1f4/128

27/08/2026 09:28:00 tunnel_traffic_utils.__exit__:
AssertionError: Did not receive expected packet on any of ports
```

### Output of `show version`

```shell
branch.202605-ars.8512e7eb-buildimage.ad6f5b869a8cacb3cb7eefe7dc226bf6f85480ff-nightly-2026.08.25.14.40
```

_No response_

linkedPullRequests.title: Fix intermittent standalone tunnel route test failure by pausing arp_update
linkedPullRequests.author: sireesha-n-arista
linkedPullRequests.body:
### Description of PR
The `test_standalone_tunnel_route` test can fail when the background
`arp_update` process runs while the test is creating an unresolved IPv6
neighbor.
In failed runs, the required tunnel route is removed while the test packets
are being sent. PTF then fails because it does not receive the expected
tunneled packet.
This change pauses `arp_update` for the whole test and starts it again during
cleanup.

Summary:
Fixes https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/issues/27701

### Type of change
- [X] Bug fix
- [ ] Testbed and Framework(new/improvement)
- [ ] New Test case
    - [ ] Skipped for non-supported platforms
- [ ] Test case improvement


### Back port request
- [ ] 202311
- [ ] 202405
- [ ] 202411
- [ ] 202505
- [ ] 202511
- [ ] 202512
- [X] 202605


### Tested branch
- [ ] master
- [ ] 202311
- [ ] 202405
- [ ] 202411
- [ ] 202505
- [ ] 202511
- [ ] 202512
- [X] 202605
- [ ] N/A

### Approach
#### What is the motivation for this PR?
The test needs full control of the neighbor state while it checks standalone
tunnel routing.
The background `arp_update` process can interfere with this state and cause
the tunnel route to be removed while packets are being sent.


#### How did you do it?
The `cleanup_neighbors` fixture now:
1. Stops `arp_update`.
2. Clears the ARP entries.
3. Clears the NDP entries.
4. Runs the test.
5. Starts `arp_update` again in a `finally` block.
Using `finally` makes sure that `arp_update` is restarted even if the test
fails.
No route-state waiting or synchronization was added.

#### How did you verify/test it?
The test was run 30 times before and after the change.
- Before the fix: 28 passed and 2 failed
- After the fix: 30 passed and 0 failed
The two failures before the fix showed the same tunnel-route
create, remove, and create-again sequence.

#### Any platform specific information?
The failure was observed on a Broadcom Dual-ToR testbed. Other platforms were
not tested.

#### Supported testbed topology if it's a new test case?
N/A

### Documentation
No documentation change is needed. This change only updates the test fixture.
